summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with hands-on embedded firmware development experience across STM32, Arduino, Raspberry Pi, and NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Built bare-metal embedded C/C++ firmware with a real-time operating system (FreeRTOS) and UART/I2C peripheral drivers, applying core computer science and software engineering fundamentals -- algorithms, debugging, and software development -- to integrate hardware and software. Comfortable in Python for tooling, with Git version control and Linux systems deployment experience.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed embedded software and firmware for a wearable gesture-recognition glove, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi over I2C and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands in Python.
Debugged and resolved sensor jitter in a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding, software calibration, and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a Python GUI (PyQt, Matplotlib) for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory hardware environment.
Used Git (GitLab) for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 embedded firmware in bare-metal C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on STM32 firmware controlling a multi-servo turret.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.
Integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization; sent control commands from Jetson-based YOLOv8 detection over UART.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) across a distributed embedded system, achieving 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection via dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux.
Deployed the Jetson-side controller as a Linux systemd service (auto-restart, non-root isolation, environment-file config) with static IP networking for reliable embedded system integration.
